Mining of coal owned by the Crow Tribe would cease. The lands subject to the leases would continue in their present condition or modified for whatever uses the surface owners may develop.
However, this may only result in a transfer of the environmental effects of mining to another location. The utilities which now receive coal from Tract III will have to find coal from other sources, and those sources are likely to be from Western mines.
Disapproval of the leases would preclude the development of a large resource owned by the Crow Tribe. The termination of mining will result in the discontinuance of annual royalties paid to the Crow Tribe as well as the employment provided by Westmoreland to Tribal members and others. The termination of mining would also preclude employment opportunities for members of the Tribe who will be entering the labor market in the future.
The economy of the surrounding communities, particularly Hardin, would be affected by a decision not to approve the leases. Adverse and beneficial socio-economic impacts described in Chapter III would not take place. Discontinuation of mining would result in the loss of about 110 jobs; the payroll losses would have an adverse effect on local businesses. Many persons employed at the existing mine probably would move elsewhere, resulting in a housing surplus and a probable decrease in property values. Projected tax revenues to the State and County would not be realized.
